title: DR1 treats an animal as identified only when every identifier its commodity asks for is filled in; the frontend accepts a record with any one of them.

finding.frontend: A person can save a cow with only an ear tag, leave the passport and tattoo boxes empty, and the record counts. That is what fe-animal-identification-saved shows: the saved row reads 'Animal 1 — Ear tag: UK123456789012' with no passport in it, and the page has moved the person on to 'Enter details for Bos taurus 2 of 2' rather than presenting the first animal again. Every identifier field is declared optional and the unit record requires just one of the six to be present (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:88-102); pressing Save and add another with all boxes empty is the only thing rejected, with the at-least-one-identifier message. Once one record exists per animal counted, the task reports itself complete.
finding.prototype: DR1 counts an animal as identified only when every field on its commodity's identifier set holds a value — a cow needs both an ear tag and a passport, a horse needs a microchip, a passport and a horse name (app/routes.js:1526-1563). A partly filled record is stored but does not count: the panel presents the same animal again with the values it already has, the entry counter does not advance, and the identification task never reports complete.
finding.difference: Raise the per-record rule from 'at least one identifier' to 'every identifier in scope for this commodity line'. That means changing the unit record's requires from anyOfIds to a rule over the in-scope identifier obligations, and moving the individual identifier obligations from optional to mandatory so each empty box names itself in the error summary rather than the record failing as a whole. Do this after the commodity identifier sets are correct, because the rule is only as good as the set it ranges over — with tattoo still on cattle it would demand a tattoo for every cow. DR1 shows no error message when a record is incomplete, so the messages are the frontend's to author.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding that DR1's identification task reports complete, or that its entry counter advances to the next animal, after a record is saved with one of its identifier fields left empty.
finding.correction: Traced on both sides and sound. DR1: isAnimalIdentifierEntryComplete (app/routes.js:1526-1532) requires every field on the set to be non-empty; hasAnimalIdentifiersComplete (:1534-1562) applies it to every saved record before the task can report complete; getSpeciesIdentificationState (:1580-1604) picks the active animal as the first index that fails it and re-presents the record with the values it already holds, so the counter genuinely does not advance; and validateAnimalIdentifiers (:1775-1785) returns an empty error list unconditionally, so DR1 really does store the partial record and say nothing. One overstatement in the frontend slot: 'pressing Save and add another with all boxes empty is the only thing rejected' is true of the single-line page in the capture but not in general — the guard at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/form/forms.js:124-135 fires only when no card anywhere on the page holds data, so on a two-commodity page an empty card is skipped silently while the filled one saves. That makes the frontend's rule weaker than the slot says, not stronger, so the finding is understated rather than wrong. Neither side's incomplete-record state is photographed; medium is the right band. SECOND PASS, after the state was captured: the frontend's half is now photographed and confidence is raised to high. fe-animal-identification-saved was shot after this finding was written and is exactly the case the finding turns on — a cow saved with an ear tag and nothing else, on a commodity whose panel offers three boxes. Two things are visible in it that were previously only read. The partial record was accepted: it appears in the saved list as 'Animal 1 — Ear tag: UK123456789012'. And the counter advanced: the open form is headed 'Enter details for Bos taurus 2 of 2', where DR1 in the same state re-presents animal 1 with the values it already holds. So the two behaviours the finding contrasts are, on the frontend side, observed rather than inferred. Being plain about what is still a source read: DR1's own incomplete-record state has not been photographed, and both limbs of the falsifier are DR1-side. The band is raised because the frontend behaviour that creates the work is now in a picture and DR1's rule was traced function by function in the first pass, not because a screenshot arrived. If a picture of DR1's side is wanted later, the state to shoot is a cattle panel with an ear tag entered, a passport left empty and the record saved.

relatedTo.why: the rule ranges over whatever identifier set the commodity has, so the sets must be right before every field becomes mandatory
